evals.prompt: We want our Cisco Duo logs in Ingext. I'm a Duo Owner and I have the Admin Panel open right now — tell me what to click, then hook it up on the Fluency side yourself.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the guided + agent-installs path: it confirms the admin holds the Owner role (only Owners can create Admin API applications), walks them through Applications → Application Catalog → Admin API → Add, has them restrict permissions to Grant read log only (unchecking every resource/application/settings/administrators grant), and collects the integration key, secret key, and API hostname while treating the secret key as a credential. It then installs the connector itself via the Fluency MCP: fetches the live Duo template with list_connector_templates, checks list_connectors for an existing instance, and calls create_connector with integrationKey, secretKey, and apiHostname plus the defaulted datalake/index parameters, instance id 'duo' (never 'default'). It verifies with list_connectors and sets the 15–30 minute first-event expectation.
expectations: The skill guides the Duo Admin Panel steps but performs the Fluency-side install itself rather than handing over instructions
It states that only an Owner-role Duo admin can create or modify the Admin API application
It restricts the application to the Grant read log permission and says to leave all other permission checkboxes unchecked
It collects the integration key, secret key, and API hostname, flagging the bare api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com hostname format
It fetches the live template schema and includes every template parameter in create_connector, with instance id derived from the template name and never 'default'
It never echoes the secret key back in summaries or output

evals.prompt: Our customer's Duo administrator is out this week, but we want everything ready for them to connect Duo to Fluency. What exactly do they need to do on their side?
evals.expected_output: The skill selects the runbook-only path: it prints the complete Duo-side procedure for the absent admin — sign in as an Owner (lesser roles cannot create Admin API applications), confirm the Duo edition includes the Admin API (Essentials/Advantage/Premier), add the Admin API application from Applications → Application Catalog, check only Grant read log and uncheck every other permission, and copy the integration key, secret key, and API hostname from the application page — and lists exactly what to send back: the three values, with the secret key handled as a secret over a secure channel. It offers to run the Fluency-side connector install as soon as those values return, and does not attempt to create anything now.
expectations: The skill recognizes the admin is absent and produces a complete vendor-side runbook instead of trying to act
The runbook covers the Owner-role requirement, the Application Catalog path, the Grant-read-log-only permission setup, and the three credential values
It clearly states the three values to report back and that the secret key is a credential
It defers the Fluency-side install until the values arrive and offers to perform it then

evals.prompt: Add Duo to Ingext. Integration key DIABC123, API hostname api-fc4422aa.duosecurity.com, and I'll paste the secret key when you ask — go.
evals.expected_output: Since the credentials are already in hand, the skill skips the Duo-side walkthrough and goes straight to the install: it collects the secret key (treating it as a credential), runs list_connector_templates for the live Duo schema, list_connectors to check for an existing instance (asking before creating a second one if present), then create_connector with application Duo, instance 'duo', displayName 'Cisco Duo Admin API', and the full parameter set including the defaulted datalake/index. It confirms the install, refers to the secret key only descriptively (never echoing it), reports the datalake index Duo for verification, and states the 15–30 minute first-event window before any row-count check.
expectations: The skill does not re-run the vendor-side walkthrough when the credentials are already provided
It checks for an existing Duo connector before installing and asks before creating a duplicate
create_connector includes every template parameter with defaults applied, instance id 'duo' rather than 'default'
The secret key is not repeated back in any confirmation or summary
It sets an honest first-event latency expectation before verifying row counts

evals.prompt: [Invoked from customer-onboarding] The customer picked Cisco Duo from the onboarding menu. The Fluency MCP is connected; the router's list_connectors call shows no Duo connector. The operator has a Duo Owner on the call. Complete this stage and hand back to the onboarding checklist.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes the onboarding hand-off: it is self-contained, so it guides the Admin API application creation and performs create_connector itself WITHOUT chaining into add-connector and without re-collecting context the router already has. On return it hands the router the connector instance id and the Duo datalake index (confirming the live table name with list_data_tables before any query), keeps the secret key out of the summary, and tells the router to expect first events within roughly 15–30 minutes — mark the application pending inside that window rather than failed.
expectations: The skill completes the connector creation itself and does not hand off to add-connector
It does not re-collect context the onboarding router already established
It hands back the instance id and datalake index for the router's verification step
The secret key does not appear in the hand-back summary
It tells the router to mark the source pending within the 15–30 minute first-event window rather than failed
